title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the solid-state lithium battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The LLTO and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The LLTO, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity during fast charging.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 96% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the interfacial resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for oxygen with improved response time
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a platinum electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the oxygen concentration. The protective layer improves the durability of the yttria-stabilized zirconia sensor in an exhaust gas. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of oxygen concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The ceramic is yttria-stabilized zirconia and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which lithium sulfide is confined in the pores of graphene to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The lithium sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid.
